headline: The night brought more bad news: US tech stocks fell hard, oil rose again to about $114, and most of Asia is down. After three falling days, Nifty starts weak and the dashboard still points down.

mood.label: Negative
mood.why: Three of four direction checks point down (bias −53 out of ±100). Overnight data as of 08:47 IST.

key_points.text: Since India closed, the Nasdaq fell **2.6%** on AI-spending and interest-rate worries, and Brent crude rose to about $113.9, its highest since May.
Asia is mostly red this morning: Japan −1.7%, Korea −2.1%, China −1.1%.
My call: the fall is **more likely to continue or stall than bounce**, with low-to-medium confidence.
FIIs (foreign investors) sold ₹3,459 crore yesterday, but Indian funds (DIIs) bought ₹2,891 crore, which keeps falls slow.
Infosys's US shares rose **3.7%** overnight, so IT stocks may hold up better.

sections.title: What changed overnight
sections.summary: Mostly worse news, which supports yesterday's fall.

points.text: US: S&P 500 fell 1.2% and Nasdaq **2.6%** after India closed, led by tech (Meta −7%). Most other US stocks rose.
US futures this morning are flat. The fall has paused, with no rebound yet.
Brent rose about 4% Thursday and 0.6% more this morning to **$113.9**, after Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. India imports most of its oil, so this hurts.
US 10-year bond rates fell 0.17 points to 4.97%. Lower US rates usually help India, but this fall came from fear.
GIFT Nifty (an early hint of the open): one tracker showed about 22,825, slightly above Nifty's 22,688 close, but sources conflict, so I couldn't confirm it.

sections.title: Bounce or continuation?
sections.summary: Continuation or a flat, nervous day looks more likely than a bounce; low-to-medium confidence.

points.text: For more falls: oil up again, Asia down, all trend checks negative, and futures traders added new bets on a fall yesterday (open positions **+4.6%** as price fell).
For a bounce: only 9.9% of FII index-futures bets are on a rise. Below 10%, FIIs have in the past rushed to close bets on a fall, lifting prices fast.
FIIs also cut option bets on a fall yesterday, an early hint their pressure may ease.
Why I lean to continuation: yesterday's fall was small (0.5%) and the put-call ratio (bets on a fall vs a rise) is a normal 0.88. Bounces usually need panic first.
I'm wrong if Nifty holds above 22,700 and heads to 22,900, or crude slips below $110.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.summary: Nifty is in a downtrend near its October lows.

points.text: Nifty (22,688) is below its 20-, 50- and 200-day averages (200-day: **24,136**), and highs and lows keep getting lower.
Dashboard scores: trend −2, positioning −1.75, option chain −0.5, put-call ratio 0. Bias **−53**: bearish, 3 of 4 agree.
India VIX (expected size of swings) is 15.8, higher than 76% of the past year: expect bigger moves both ways. Next support is the 22,180–22,220 lows.

sections.title: What big investors are doing
sections.summary: Foreign investors keep selling; Indian funds keep buying almost as much.

points.text: FIIs sold ₹3,459 crore yesterday and **₹38,171 crore** so far in October.
DIIs bought ₹2,891 crore yesterday and ₹40,652 crore this month, more than FIIs sold.
FIIs still hold about 280,000 more index-futures contracts betting on a fall than a rise, and added a few more yesterday.

sections.title: What the world is telling India
sections.summary: Costly oil and a Fed that may raise rates again are the main pressures.

points.text: Brent is up **14%** in a month. Costlier oil means higher prices, a weaker rupee and lower company profits.
The rupee closed weak at 94.82 per dollar, down 36 paise, which puts off foreign investors.
Fed decision on 28–29 October: markets see about a 93% chance of no change, but a rate rise by December as very likely.
Gold fell 2.5% Thursday. India imports a lot of gold, so this slightly helps the rupee.

sections.title: Company results
sections.summary: Most big results are good, but the market punishes anything below hopes.

points.text: Bajaj Finance profit rose 28.7%; the stock gained about 3% yesterday. ICICI Bank (+21.4%) and UltraTech (+21.3%) were also strong.
Eternal's profit nearly doubled to ₹125 crore, but missed one broker's ₹293 crore estimate. Stock fell about **2.5%**.
HDFC Bank's profit grew only 5.6%; shares fell 1.8% and its US listing 1% more overnight.

sections.title: What could change the picture
sections.summary: Oil, the Fed and Tuesday's monthly expiry matter most.

points.text: Middle East news: fresh attacks on Gulf oil push crude up; calm would bring the fastest relief.
Monthly expiry on **Tuesday 27 October**: prices can swing as traders close bets. L&T, Maruti and Tata Steel report that day; Kotak Bank on Saturday.
Fed decision early Thursday 29 October (Indian time). A December rate-rise hint could add to FII selling.

levels.note: A close above 23,000 would weaken the downtrend; below 22,500 opens the way to the 22,200 lows.

watch.text: The open vs yesterday's 22,688. A gap down that keeps falling would confirm the call.
Brent crude: back below $110 would ease pressure.
US business surveys (PMI). Strong numbers could raise Fed rate-rise fears.
Provisional FII and DII figures after the close.

bottom_line: The trend is down, FIIs are still selling, and the night added more worry: weak US tech, oil near $114 and falling Asian markets. The dashboard is bearish with medium conviction (−53, 3 of 4 checks agree), and I lean towards the fall continuing or stalling today. The main risk is FIIs suddenly closing their very large bets on a fall, which could lift Nifty fast, especially if oil eases.
